body.text: Āps 1. bhagavāṃc chrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma. icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ satvānām
body.translated_text: [Āps 1] The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta</s>'s Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Do you wish, monks, to hear about the limit of the lifespan of beings

body.text: āyuḥparyantaṃ śrotuṃ. etasya bhagavāṃ kāla, etasya sugata samayo, yad bhagavān bhikṣūṇāṃ satvānām āyuḥparyantaṃ deśayed. bhagavataḥ śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti. tena hi bhikṣavaḥ
body.translated_text: ?' 'This is the [right] time, <s>Bhagavān</s>; this is the [right] occasion, <s>Sugata</s>, for the <s>Bhagavān</s> to teach the monks about the limit of the lifespan of beings. Having heard from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the monks will retain [the teaching].' 'Then, monks,

body.text:
śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta, bhāṣiṣya. evaṃ bhadanteti. te bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pratyaśroṣuḥ. atha bhagavāṃs tān bhikṣūn idam avocat*.
Āps 2. paraṃ bhikṣavo narakeṣu kalpa āyuṣaḥ
body.translated_text: listen well and pay careful attention; I shall speak.' 'Yes, Venerable One.' Those monks assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to those monks: [Āps 2] 'The maximum measure of lifespan in the hells, monks, is a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age);

body.text:
pramāṇam, asty antareṇa kālakriyā.
Āps 3. paraṃ bhikṣavas tiryakṣu kalpa āyuṣaḥ pramāṇam, asty antareṇa kālakriyā.
Āps 4. yāni bhikṣavo manuṣyāṇāṃ triṃśad rātriṃdivasāni tat pretānām
body.translated_text: there is [the possibility of] death in the interim. [Āps 3] The maximum measure of lifespan among animals, monks, is a <s>kalpa</s>; there is death in the interim. [Āps 4] What is thirty days and nights for human beings, monks, is one day and night for the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts);

body.text: ekaṃ rātriṃdivasaṃ, tena rātriṃdivasena triṃśad rātrakeṇa māsena, dvādaśa māsakena saṃvatsareṇa, tayā saṃvatsaragaṇanayā paṃca varṣaśatāni pretānām āyuṣaḥ
body.translated_text: by that day and night, with a month of thirty nights, and a year of twelve months, by that reckoning of years, five hundred years is the measure of the lifespan of the <s>pretas</s>.

body.text:

Āps 5. atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthā bhāṣate.
  viśuṣkakaṇṭhauṣṭhapuṭā
body.translated_text: That amounts, by human reckoning, to fifteen thousand years as the measure of lifespan; there is death in the interim. [Āps 5] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke these verses: With dried-up throats and lips,

children.translated_text: with towering forms like mighty mountains,
covered by their own hair, with mouths gaping open,
thin, with nostrils as fine as needles. //1//

body.translated_text: Naked, covered by their own hair, with skeleton-like bodies,
with skulls in their hands, terrifying, wailing, running about. //2//
Crying out with voices of distress, they experience painful sensation. //3//

body.text: utpannās te pretaloke karma kṛtveha pāpakaḥ // 4
body.translated_text: they have been reborn in the realm of <s>pretas</s>, having done evil <s>karma</s> here. //4//

body.text: Āps 6. pūrvavidehakānāṃ bhikṣavo manuṣyāṇām ardhatritīyāni varṣaśatāny āyuṣaḥ pramāṇam, asty antareṇa
body.translated_text: [Āps 6] The measure of the lifespan of the humans of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, monks, is two hundred and fifty years; there is death in the interim.

Āps 8. uttarakauravāṇāṃ bhikṣavo manuṣyāṇāṃ varṣasahasrāṇy āyuṣaḥ
body.translated_text: [Āps 7] The measure of the lifespan of the humans of <s>Avaragodānīya</s>, monks, is five hundred years; there is death in the interim. [Āps 8] The measure of the lifespan of the humans of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, monks, is a thousand years;

body.text:

Āps 9. kena kāraṇenottarakauravāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ varṣasahasram āyuṣaḥ pramāṇam, nāsty antareṇa kālakriyā.
Āps 10. uttarakauravā bhikṣavo
body.translated_text: there is no death in the interim. [Āps 9] For what reason is the measure of the lifespan of the humans of <s>Uttarakuru</s> a thousand years, with no death in the interim? [Āps 10] The humans of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, monks,

body.translated_text: increase and decrease [of lifespan] are observed. The humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, monks, [live] for an immeasurable lifespan, or for eighty thousand years,

śatāyuṣo 'pi, daśavarṣāyuṣo 'pi.

body.translated_text: or for a hundred years, or for ten years. [Āps 13] At present, monks, the measure of the lifespan of the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is a hundred years. At present, monks,

Āps 14. varṣaśataṃ khalu bhikṣavo jīvaṃ daśāvasthāḥ pratyanubhavati. prathamāyām avasthāyāṃ
body.translated_text: among the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, whoever lives long lives a hundred years, or slightly more, when properly and comfortably maintained. [Āps 14] Living a hundred years, monks, one experiences ten stages. In the first stage,
one is a baby — helpless, lying on one's back. In the second

body.text: yām avasthāyāṃ kumāro bhavati krīḍanajātīyaḥ. tṛtīyāyām avasthāyāṃ yuvā bhavati kāmabhogī. caturthyām avasthāyāṃ
body.translated_text: stage, one is a boy — inclined to play. In the third stage, one is a youth — enjoying sensual pleasures. In the fourth stage,

body.text: balavān bhavati utsāhī. paṃcamyām avasthāyāṃ prajño bhavati pratibhānavān*. ṣaṣṭhyām avasthāyāṃ smṛtimān bhavati mīmāṃsanajātīyaḥ. saptamyām avasthāyāṃ sthito bhavati manā
body.translated_text: one is strong — full of energy. In the fifth stage, one is wise — possessed of ready wit. In the sixth stage, one is mindful — inclined to investigation. In the seventh stage, one is steadfast —

body.text: + + prāptaḥ. aṣṭhamyām avasthāyāṃ sthaviro bhavati rājanyaḥ. navamyām avasthāyāṃ vṛddho bhavati jarājīrṇaḥ. daśamyām avasthāyāṃ gatāyur bhavati maraṇaparāyaṇaḥ. varṣaśa
body.translated_text: [having] attained [maturity]. In the eighth stage, one is an elder — venerable. In the ninth stage, one is old — worn out by age. In the tenth stage, one's lifespan is spent — destined for death. Living a hundred
